sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Energy and Technology continue to anchor a highly bifurcated market where six of eleven sectors maintain all-green momentum, despite a complete freeze in short-term sector rotation.

Market breadth remains constructive with a majority (6 of 11) of sectors holding "all-green" status across all timeframes. Energy leads the pack with a momentum score of 0.92 (rank 1 YTD), closely followed by Technology at 0.88, which stands out as the only sector exhibiting sustained top-three strength across the 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons. 

In contrast, short-term momentum has completely stalled, with zero rank changes across all sectors over the last five sessions. While defensive and cyclical laggards like Consumer Cyclical (0.17 momentum) and Communication Services (0.15 momentum) remain pinned at the bottom, a low-agreement divergence in Financials suggests the broader rally's foundation may be starting to crack.

## Strength
* **Constructive Breadth:** Six out of eleven market groups—Energy, Technology, Healthcare, Industrials, Financial, and Real Estate—are currently "all-green," demonstrating positive performance across weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and YTD timeframes.
* **Sustained Tech Leadership:** Technology is the sole sector to maintain a top-three rank across 1-month, 3-month, and 6-month periods, backed by a strong momentum score of 0.88 (YTD Rank 2).
* **Energy Dominance:** Energy holds the absolute top spot in momentum at 0.92 (YTD Rank 1), anchoring the market's leading groups.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Stalled Rotation:** Sector momentum has completely locked in place, with all tracked sectors—including Basic Materials (rank 4, momentum 0.52), Industrials (rank 3, momentum 0.63), and Healthcare (rank 8, momentum 0.67)—registering zero rank movement (+0 spots) over the last five sessions.
* **Momentum Leaders:** Behind Energy (0.917) and Technology (0.883), Healthcare (0.667) and Industrials (0.633) round out the top tier of positive momentum.
* **Deep Laggards:** Communication Services (0.150 momentum, YTD Rank 10) and Consumer Cyclical (0.167 momentum, YTD Rank 11) continue to drag at the bottom of the performance spectrum.

## Divergences
* **Fragile Financials:** Despite holding an "all-green" profile, Financials (momentum 0.58, YTD Rank 6) exhibit a low agreement score of 0.47, signaling that its current strength is unstable and prone to rank degradation.
* **Real Estate Disconnect:** Real Estate remains in the all-green camp with a momentum score of 0.47, yet it sits on the edge of the laggard territory (YTD Rank 5), indicating a widening performance gap among the all-green groups.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Secular leaders in energy refining and tech hardware maintain absolute dominance, but a powerful defensive rotation is underway as commodities and health tech surge while luxury and consumer discretionary groups collapse.

US equity market breadth remains highly concentrated, with only 24 of 144 industry groups achieving "all-green" status across all timeframes. Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (momentum 0.983) and Computer Hardware (momentum 0.970) continue to anchor the market as the leading YTD performers. However, capital is aggressively rotating into defensive and commodity-linked pockets. Health Information Services has emerged as a primary beneficiary of this rotation, surging 38 spots to rank 51 with a momentum score of 0.80, alongside notable gains in Aerospace & Defense (+27 spots) and Gold (+24 spots).

Conversely, premium consumer and interest-sensitive groups are fading rapidly. Luxury Goods suffered a severe de-rating, plunging 71 spots to rank 113 with a weak 0.20 momentum score. Regulated Water Utilities (-32 spots) and Consumer Electronics (-15 spots) also experienced steep weekly declines, reflecting a sharp risk-off pivot away from premium discretionary spend and yield-sensitive plays.

## Strength
* **Concentrated Leadership:** Only 16.7% of the market (24 of 144 groups) exhibits clean positive trends across weekly, monthly, quarterly, half-year, and YTD horizons. 
* **Sustained Heavyweights:** Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.98 momentum) and Computer Hardware (0.97 momentum) remain the market's strongest pillars, holding sustained top-36 rankings over the last 1, 3, and 6 months.
* **All-Green Cohort:** Staffing & Employment Services (0.91 momentum), Health Information Services (0.80 momentum), and Steel (0.80 momentum) lead the broader group of 24 all-green industries.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Velocity Leaders:** Health Information Services led all weekly gainers (+38 spots, rank 51), followed by Aerospace & Defense (+27 spots, rank 83) and Gold (+24 spots, rank 87).
* **Sharpest De-ratings:** Luxury Goods collapsed by 71 spots to rank 113, while Utilities - Regulated Water fell 32 spots to rank 99 (momentum 0.16).
* **Momentum Anchors:** Advertising Agencies (0.017 momentum, YTD rank 144) and Airports & Air Services (0.055 momentum, YTD rank 138) remain the weakest performing industries in the market.

## Divergences
* **Emerging Turnarounds:** Uranium (+21 spots, momentum 0.48) and Utilities - Renewable (+15 spots, momentum 0.50) are climbing rapidly in rank despite low absolute momentum scores, signaling early-stage trend reversals.
* **Negative Divergences:** Metal Fabrication (momentum 0.73) and Department Stores (momentum 0.64) are showing signs of exhaustion, slipping 7 and 5 spots respectively over the last 5 sessions despite high momentum scores.
* **Fragile Leaders:** Despite holding all-green status, Scientific & Technical Instruments and Semiconductors exhibit low trend agreement (0.49), pointing to highly unstable underlying rank structures.
